evidence.draft: This course introduces students to the vital role of computers and computer programmers in shaping modern society. It aims to foster a strong foundation in logical formulation techniques essential for programming, while promoting the development of good coding practices. Students will be taught the fundamentals of Java programming: program structure and the JDK/JVM, console and file input/output, variables, data types and operators, conditional statements, loops, arrays, strings, methods and recursion, and connecting a Java program to a database. They will apply these to real-world problems. In line with La Consolacion University Philippines' commitment to forming Christo-centric Catholic professionals, the course integrates Marian Augustinian values in each lesson, ensuring that students not only achieve intellectual growth but also cultivate moral and ethical responsibility in the digital age. This holistic approach nurtures individuals who contribute positively to society, embodying community, humility, and love of service, as exemplified by the Blessed Virgin Mary and Saint Augustine. By the end of the course, students will have created their own Java applications, including a database-connected program, demonstrating both technical proficiency and a sense of purpose rooted in their Catholic faith.

ilos.text: ILO 1: Explain the course structure and expectations and identify the computing requirements of a simple real-world IT problem that Java programming can address, citing professional ethical standards.

actual.contents:
I. Orientation
A. Introduction to the Course Contents and Course Requirements and Activities
B. Course Objectives, Grading System and Policies on Absences, Tardiness and Examinations
C. Overview of key Java programming concepts (program, source code, compiler, variables, control structures)
D. How programming skills address real-world IT challenges
E. Professional ethical standards in programming
actual.activities:
• Setting and sharing of Expectations from the Course
• Discussion on the Vision, Mission and Goals of LCUP and of CITE
• Presentation of Course Objectives and Contents, Course Requirements and Activities, and Review of Policies on Absences, Tardiness, Examinations and Grading System
• Short guided discussion where students explain, in their own words, what Java is used for and how programming addresses real-world IT challenges
• Small-group discussion of a case on professional ethical standards in programming
actual.tasks:
• Statement of Expectations
• Review of Course Contents, Objectives, Activities and Assessment Tools
• Review of Policies on Absences, Tardiness, Examinations, Grading System
• Short written reflection explaining key Java programming concepts, one real-world IT challenge Java can address, and one professional ethical standard for programmers
actual.values:
• Courage – students voice their honest expectations and questions about the course when they share and review it
• Humility – students listen to classmates' expectations and accept the course policies on absences, tardiness and examinations
• Community-orientedness – students commit to shared class norms and recognize how the LCUP and CITE vision and mission guide their work in IT

ilos.text: LO1. Explain the basic concepts and principles of Java programming that are needed to define the computing requirements of a solution.

actual.contents:
II. Introduction to Java Programming
• A Brief History of Java language
• Characteristics of Java Language
• Reasons why programmers use Java language, Features of Java Programming
• Basic concepts and principles: structure of a Java program, compiling and running (JDK, JVM, bytecode), basic syntax, variables and data types, and introduction to object-oriented principles
• Worked examples of simple Java programs explained line by line
actual.activities:
• Lecture-Discussion with recitation using PowerPoint Presentation, where students explain Java concepts in their own words
• Video Presentation on how Java programs are written and run
• Discovery Learning: students explore and run simple Java programs and describe how the basic concepts work
• Functioning Knowledge: students explain Java principles to a partner using examples
actual.tasks:
• Brain Storming: class list of Java features and basic concepts
• Quiz: short questions in which students explain basic Java concepts and principles (program structure, syntax, data types, object-oriented principles)
• Assignment: written explanation of how a simple Java program works, citing the basic concepts it uses
actual.values:
• Courage – students volunteer to explain Java concepts aloud in recitation and brainstorming, even when unsure
• Humility – students accept correction on quizzes and assignments and learn from classmates' explanations of Java principles
• Community-orientedness – students help one another understand the basic concepts through partner explanations

ilos.text: ILO1: Analyze the computing requirements of a simple problem and identify the Java syntax and semantics (variables, constants, operators, console input/output) needed to meet them.
ILO2: Apply basic Java programming concepts through hands-on practice by working with classmates from different backgrounds to build a simple program that addresses a community need.

actual.contents:
III. The Basic Input/Output Statements of Java Console
• Java installation and setting up the Eclipse IDE
• Basic input/output statements, with worked examples using Scanner and System.out
• Variable declaration, rules for naming variables, and the meaning (semantics) of assignment
• Constants and operators (arithmetic, relational, logical), with traced examples of how expressions are evaluated
• Worked console programs that combine input, variables and operators
actual.activities:
• Discussion of Java syntax and semantics using PowerPoint
• Instructor demonstration of writing and running a console program in Eclipse
• Guided hands-on coding: students type, run and trace programs that use variables, constants, operators and input/output
• Discovery learning: students predict and then test the output of short code snippets
• Pair debugging of syntax errors
actual.tasks:
• Machine Problem: write and run a Java console program that declares variables and constants, reads user input and computes results with operators, graded on correct syntax and output
• Quiz: short items on syntax rules and tracing the output of code snippets (semantics)
• Recitation/group participation: explain a code snippet's behaviour aloud
• Assignment: correct the syntax and logic errors in a given program and explain each fix
actual.values:
• Interiority: students reflect on their own coding habits and on honesty in doing their machine problems, writing and explaining their own code rather than copying.
• Courage: students try new Java syntax, run programs that may fail, and present and explain their code and errors in recitation.

ilos.text: ILO 1: Analyze the data input and output requirements of a problem and apply Java streams to read and write data that meets them.
ILO 2 Acquire the necessary skills and understanding of java methods.
ILO 4: Apply the syntax and semantics of Java to write working programs with a classmate for a simple community-related problem.

actual.contents:
IV. Java Libraries Program
• Parts of a Java program
• The print and println function
• Data types: int, float, double, char
• Reasons to declare variables
• Java streams: InputStream/OutputStream and Reader/Writer classes
• Reading input with Scanner and writing output to the console and to a text file
• Worked example: tracing data read from a file, processed, and written to a new file
• Handling input errors responsibly
actual.activities:
• Lecture-Discussion using PowerPoint presentation on Java streams
• Seatwork: trace code that reads and writes data with streams
• Laboratory: write a Java program that reads data from the keyboard or a file using streams and writes results to a file
• Machine Problem Video Presentation: demonstrate and explain the stream-based program
actual.tasks:
• Recitation on how Java streams read and write data
• Laboratory exercise: submit a Java program that reads records from a text file and writes a processed report to another file, graded with a rubric on correct stream use and output
actual.values:
• Humility: students ask for and give help when debugging, and accept corrections to their syntax errors in the laboratory.
• Community-orientedness: students share working code and explain it to classmates during the Machine Problem Video Presentation.
• Interiority: students reflect on whether their program is honest and careful work.

ilos.text: Review topics covered by the examination

actual.activities: Examination on the topics discussed during the Prelim Term

ilos.text: ILO3: Analyze the requirements of a given problem and explain how structured logic (decisions, loops, and array manipulation) can be used to meet them.

ILO4: Be able to apply conditional statements in Java to control program flow based on specific conditions, and write programs that make decisions dynamically depending on user input or computed values, applying ethical standards such as honest, fair, and safe handling of input so the program serves the common good.

actual.contents:
V. Structured Logic in Java
• Conditional Statements: syntax, if statement, if-else statement, switch/case, with sample programs that trace which branch runs
• Looping Constructs: for, while, do-while, with traced examples of repeated tasks
• Arrays: declaring, accessing and traversing arrays with loops, with worked examples combining decisions, loops, and arrays
actual.activities:
• Discussion using PowerPoint Presentation on decisions, loops, and arrays
• Video Presentation on structured logic in Java
• Laboratory Exercises: tracing and explaining short Java programs that use if/else, loops, and arrays, done in pairs or small groups
actual.tasks:
• Recitation: explaining how decisions, loops, and arrays control program flow
• Seatwork: tracing code that uses if/else, loops, and arrays and stating the output
• Laboratory Exercises: short Java programs using decisions, loops, and arrays, with a written explanation of the logic
actual.values:
• Humility: students accept feedback from peers and the instructor when their conditional logic gives wrong output, and fix their code.
• Courage: students attempt and defend their own Java solutions for decision-making programs during recitation and laboratory exercises, even when unsure.
• Community-orientedness: students work in pairs or groups in the laboratory exercises, sharing code reviews so everyone can write correct conditional programs.

ilos.text: ILO1: Analyze the requirements of a repetitive real-world task and utilize looping constructs (for, while, do-while) in Java to design programs that efficiently handle repetitive processes and iterations.
ILO2. Inference the structured programming concepts aCLOng with the Java syntax to implement them.

actual.contents:
XI. Looping Statements
• Java Loops
▪ For Loops
▪ While Loops
▪ Do While Loop
▪ Break/Continue
• Choosing the right loop for a task and avoiding infinite loops
• Nested loops and worked examples
• Worked examples: applying loops to real-world problems (e.g., totals, averages, menus, patterns)
actual.activities:
• Discussion using PowerPoint Presentation on for, while and do-while loops
• Laboratory Exercises: students write and run Java programs using for, while and do-while loops to handle repetitive tasks
• Students design and code a loop-based program that solves a real-world problem (e.g., grade computation, ATM menu)
actual.tasks:
• Recitation on loop concepts
• Group Participation in laboratory work
• Quiz on loop syntax and tracing loop output
• Machine Problem: write a Java program using for, while and do-while loops to solve a real-world repetitive problem, graded on correctness and efficiency
actual.values:
• Humility: students admit and correct errors in their loops (such as infinite loops) during laboratory exercises and accept classmates' feedback.
• Community-orientedness: in group participation, students help one another debug loop programs in the Machine Problem.
• Interiority: students reflect on the precision and accuracy their code needs.

ilos.text: Review topics covered by the examination

actual.activities: Examination on the topics discussed during the Midterm Term

ilos.text: ILO4: Analyze the data storage requirements of a problem and declare, initialize, and manipulate one-dimensional and multi-dimensional arrays in Java to store, retrieve, and process data in various applications.
ILO6: Synthesize skills in De-bugging Java Language program.

actual.contents:
X. Arrays
• One-dimensional arrays: declaration and initialization
• Accessing, storing and retrieving elements
• Processing arrays with loops (traversal, sum, search)
• Two-dimensional arrays: syntax, declaration, initialization and processing
• Worked examples of arrays in applications (e.g., grades, seating chart)
actual.activities:
• Discussion using PowerPoint presentation on one-dimensional and two-dimensional arrays
• Guided discovery learning: students declare and initialize arrays and trace their contents
• Laboratory exercises: students write Java programs that store, retrieve and process data (searching, summing, sorting) in one-dimensional and multi-dimensional arrays
• Short quiz on array syntax
actual.tasks:
• Recitation
• Quiz on error types and debugging techniques
• Machine problem: students debug given faulty Java console programs (including array programs), submit the corrected code and a short debugging log explaining each error and its fix
actual.values:
• Compassion: while debugging array programs in the laboratory, students patiently help classmates find and fix errors and give kind, constructive feedback
• Humility: students admit their own coding mistakes and learn from corrections as they work toward the array and debugging ILOs

ilos.text: ILO1: Analyze the text-processing requirements of a problem and apply suitable Java string manipulation methods to meet them.
LO2: Synthesize debugging skills by collaborating with classmates from diverse backgrounds to find and fix errors in Java programs that address a social challenge.

actual.contents:
XIII. Strings
• String basics and immutability
• String manipulation methods with worked Java examples: length(), charAt(), indexOf(), concat(), replace(), equalsIgnoreCase(), toLowerCase()/toUpperCase(), substring()
• Applying the methods to everyday tasks (validating input, extracting parts of text, formatting names)
actual.activities:
Lecture:
• Discussion using PowerPoint Presentation on common Java errors and debugging techniques
• Quiz
• Laboratory Exercises: students are given faulty Java String programs, trace and locate the errors, fix them and re-test (Machine Problem)
• Seatwork using trial and error discovery learning: students debug and improve their own Java programs and explain each fix
actual.tasks:
• Recitation on string methods
• Quiz on the behaviour of length(), charAt(), indexOf(), concat(), replace() and substring()
• Seatwork (trial and error discovery learning): students write Java programs that manipulate strings
• Accurate program output: working Java programs that correctly apply the string manipulation methods
actual.values:
• Humility: students admit and learn from their own coding errors and accept classmates' feedback when debugging String programs
• Courage: students run, test and try fixes on faulty Java code without fear of failure, and present their solutions in recitation
• Patience and critical thinking: students trace their code step by step through trial and error until the output is correct

ilos.text: ILO4: Analyze the requirements of a given problem and demonstrate the Java syntax and semantics needed to meet them.
ILO5: Build robust Java console applications that meet computing requirements the student has defined and analyzed.
ILO6: Synthesize debugging skills for Java programs by collaborating with diverse teammates to find and fix errors in a Java solution that addresses a social challenge.

actual.contents:
XII. JAVA METHODS
• Method syntax: declaring and calling methods, return types
• Java parameters: how arguments are passed and what a method returns (semantics), with traced examples
• Methods calling other methods and objects
• Java recursion: base case and recursive case, with worked examples and output tracing
actual.activities:
• Discussion using PowerPoint Presentation on Java method syntax, parameters and recursion
• Blended Learning: online practice on writing Java methods
• Quiz on the discussed topic
• Laboratory Exercises: students write, run and trace Java methods with parameters and recursion, and explain what each program does
actual.tasks:
• Recitation: explain the syntax and the output of given Java methods
• Quiz on Java method syntax, parameters and recursion
• Machine problem: hands-on exercises writing Java programs with methods, parameters and recursion, graded on correct syntax and accurate output
actual.values:
• Interiority: during debugging in the laboratory exercises, students reflect honestly on their own mistakes and how they approached the problem before changing the code.
• Courage: students present and defend their Java console application in recitation and admit and fix errors found by peers, rather than hiding them.

ilos.text: ILO1: Retrieve data from a relational database using a Java class, working with teammates to build a Java solution that addresses a social challenge.
Demonstrate the Filipino-Catholic Augustinian Spirituality through value webbing.

actual.contents:
X. JAVA DATABASE CONNECTION
• Improvised Database UCanAccess Connection
Value webbing: Filipino-Catholic Augustinian Spirituality (community, humility, love of service) linked to responsible handling of stored data, with a sample value web connecting database use to the common good
actual.activities:
• Discussion using PowerPoint on Augustinian values in responsible data handling
• Cooperative learning: groups create a value web linking Filipino-Catholic Augustinian Spirituality (community, humility, love of service) to their database program
• Group presentation of the value web
• Group Dynamics Laboratory Exercises on Java database connection
actual.tasks:
• Recitation
• Quiz
• Value web output: each group submits a value web showing how Filipino-Catholic Augustinian Spirituality (community, humility, love of service) applies to their database program, graded with a rubric
• Machine problem: hands-on exercises using Java programs
actual.values:
• Community-orientedness: students work in groups on the database laboratory exercises and the value web, sharing code and helping one another.
• Courage: students try retrieving data from a database, face connection errors and debug them, and present their value web.
• Humility: students accept peer feedback on their code and value web.

judgements.label: NOT_ALIGNED
judgements.explanation: The PO asks to articulate and discuss (Understand/Analyze) the latest developments in the field. The CLO is about analyzing requirements and designing Java solutions. It has no verb of articulating or discussing, and nothing about current developments or trends in computing. It only shares the general computing field.
judgements.sourceQuote: Articulate and discuss the latest developments in the specific field of practice
judgements.targetQuote: Analyze and define the computing requirements needed for an effective solution
judgements.draft: Analyze and define the computing requirements needed for an effective solution, and discuss current developments in Java and computing practice that inform original, holistic and impactful Java-based designs.

judgements.label: NOT_ALIGNED
judgements.explanation: The PO asks for oral and written communication in English and Filipino. The CLO has no communication verb, no oral or written product, and no mention of English or Filipino.
judgements.sourceQuote: Effectively communicate orally and in writing using both English and Filipino
judgements.targetQuote: Analyze and define the computing requirements needed for an effective solution
judgements.draft: Analyze and define the computing requirements needed for an effective solution, and communicate the resulting original Java-based design orally and in writing in English and Filipino.

judgements.label: NOT_ALIGNED
judgements.explanation: The PO is about working effectively and independently in multi-disciplinary, multi-cultural teams. The CLO describes individual analysis and design with no teamwork, independence, or multi-disciplinary or cultural context. That competency is in CLO 3, not here.
judgements.sourceQuote: Work effectively and independently in multi-disciplinary and multi-cultural teams
judgements.targetQuote: creatively design original Java-based solutions that are holistic and impactful
judgements.draft: Analyze and define the computing requirements needed for an effective solution, and creatively design original Java-based solutions that are holistic and impactful, working effectively and independently within multi-disciplinary and multi-cultural teams.

judgements.label: ALIGNED
judgements.explanation: The CLO analyzes and defines computing requirements for a solution, matching the PO's verbs, level and subject.
judgements.sourceQuote: Analyze complex problems, and identify and define the computing requirements
judgements.targetQuote: Analyze and define the computing requirements needed for an effective solution

judgements.label: PARTIALLY_ALIGNED
judgements.explanation: The CLO designs Java solutions (Create), which matches the PO's design verb. It does not show develop or implement, and nothing signals a system-level perspective. The word 'holistic' is vague and does not state system-level thinking.
judgements.sourceQuote: Design and develop computing solutions using a system-level perspective
judgements.targetQuote: creatively design original Java-based solutions that are holistic and impactful
judgements.draft: Analyze and define the computing requirements needed for an effective solution, and creatively design and develop original Java-based solutions using a system-level perspective that are holistic and impactful.

judgements.label: ALIGNED
judgements.explanation: Analyzing requirements and creatively designing original solutions shows critical and creative thinking.
judgements.sourceQuote: Critical and Creative thinker
judgements.targetQuote: Analyze and define the computing requirements

judgements.label: PARTIALLY_ALIGNED
judgements.explanation: The CLO only says solutions are 'holistic and impactful'. It names no social responsibility, stewardship, community need or common good, so it does not show a socially responsive steward. It also lacks any verb of acting responsibly toward society.
judgements.sourceQuote: Socially Responsive Steward
judgements.targetQuote: holistic and impactful
judgements.draft: Analyze and define the computing requirements needed for an effective solution, and creatively design original Java-based solutions that are holistic and impactful and responsibly serve the needs of the community and the common good.

judgements.label: NOT_ALIGNED
judgements.explanation: The EGA is about lifelong learning and transformation. The CLO has no learning-to-learn, reflection, self-directed growth or continuous improvement element, and only concerns a single design task.
judgements.sourceQuote: Transformative Lifelong learner
judgements.targetQuote: Analyze and define the computing requirements needed for an effective solution
judgements.draft: Analyze and define the computing requirements needed for an effective solution, and creatively design original Java-based solutions that are holistic and impactful, reflecting on and continually improving one's own programming practice as a lifelong learner.

judgements.label: ALIGNED

judgements.sourceQuote: Analyze complex problems, and identify and define the computing requirements
judgements.targetQuote: Analyze and define the computing requirements needed for an effective solution

judgements.sourceQuote: Critical and Creative thinker
judgements.targetQuote: creatively design original Java-based solutions

judgements.targetQuote: Incorporate ethical standards and social responsibility into technical designs

judgements.targetQuote: into technical designs, ensuring that solutions serve the common good

judgements.targetQuote: Incorporate ethical standards and social responsibility into technical designs

judgements.label: PARTIALLY_ALIGNED
judgements.explanation: The contents cover declaring, initializing, accessing and processing 1D and 2D arrays with worked examples. Nothing teaches how to analyze a problem's data storage requirements (what data, how many values, which dimensions), so the ILO's Analyze verb is not covered.

judgements.targetQuote: Worked examples of arrays in applications (e.g., grades, seating chart)

• Accessing, storing and retrieving elements

• Two-dimensional arrays: syntax, declaration, initialization and processing
• Worked examples of arrays in applications (e.g., grades, seating chart)
• Common errors in array programs (syntax, runtime such as ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException, and logic errors) and debugging techniques (reading error messages, tracing, test cases)
• Worked example: debugging a faulty array program and re-testing the fix

judgements.label: PARTIALLY_ALIGNED
judgements.explanation: The laboratory exercises have students write array programs that store, retrieve and process data, which practises declare, initialize and manipulate. No activity has students analyze a problem's data storage requirements, so the Analyze verb is not practised.

judgements.label: PARTIALLY_ALIGNED

judgements.targetQuote: apply suitable Java string manipulation methods to meet them

judgements.label: PARTIALLY_ALIGNED
judgements.explanation: The contents cover the string methods with worked examples and everyday applications. Nothing shows how to analyze a text-processing requirement (identify inputs, outputs and which method fits), so the Analyze part of the ILO is not covered.

judgements.targetQuote: Applying the methods to everyday tasks (validating input, extracting parts of text, formatting names)

• Applying the methods to everyday tasks (validating input, extracting parts of text, formatting names)

judgements.label: PARTIALLY_ALIGNED
judgements.explanation: The activities are mostly about debugging faulty String programs, which touches string methods. No activity has students analyze a text-processing requirement. judgements.targetQuote: students are given faulty Java String programs, trace and locate the errors, fix them and re-test

judgements.label: PARTIALLY_ALIGNED

• Accurate program output: working Java programs that correctly apply the string manipulation methods to meet the stated requirement

judgements.label: PARTIALLY_ALIGNED
judgements.explanation: The contents teach String methods but contain nothing on debugging: no common errors, no tracing or testing techniques, no finding and fixing of faulty code. The Create-level 'synthesize' is not reached, because the examples only show applying methods. There is nothing on collaboration or peer feedback with diverse classmates. The programs are everyday tasks, not a social challenge.
judgements.sourceQuote: find and fix errors in Java programs that address a social challenge
judgements.targetQuote: Applying the methods to everyday tasks (validating input, extracting parts of text, formatting names)
judgements.draft:
XIII. Strings
• String basics and immutability
• String manipulation methods with worked Java examples: length(), charAt(), indexOf(), concat(), replace(), equalsIgnoreCase(), toLowerCase()/toUpperCase(), substring()
• Applying the methods to everyday tasks (validating input, extracting parts of text, formatting names)
• Common String errors and how to debug them: off-by-one mistakes with charAt()/substring(), StringIndexOutOfBoundsException, == versus equals(), forgetting immutability; reading error messages, tracing, print statements, re-testing
• Worked example: finding and fixing errors in a faulty String program that serves a social cause (e.g., validating names in a community registry form)
• Peer debugging in diverse teams: sharing, explaining and accepting feedback on fixes

The faulty programs are generic String programs and are not tied to any social challenge. The 'synthesize' level is only partly reached.

judgements.targetQuote: students are given faulty Java String programs, trace and locate the errors, fix them and re-test

judgements.label: PARTIALLY_ALIGNED

judgements.targetQuote: Students will be taught the fundamentals of Java programming and explore significant real-world applications.
judgements.draft: This course introduces students to the vital role of computers and computer programmers in shaping modern society. It aims to foster a strong foundation in logical formulation techniques essential for programming, while promoting the development of good coding practices. Students will be taught the fundamentals of Java programming: program structure and the JDK/JVM, console and file input/output, variables, data types and operators, conditional statements, loops, arrays, strings, methods and recursion, and connecting a Java program to a database. They will apply these to real-world problems. In line with La Consolacion University Philippines' commitment to forming Christo-centric Catholic professionals, the course integrates Marian Augustinian values in each lesson, ensuring that students not only achieve intellectual growth but also cultivate moral and ethical responsibility in the digital age. This holistic approach nurtures individuals who contribute positively to society, embodying community, humility, and love of service, as exemplified by the Blessed Virgin Mary and Saint Augustine. By the end of the course, students will have created their own Java applications, including a database-connected program, demonstrating both technical proficiency and a sense of purpose rooted in their Catholic faith.

suggestions.title: Suggested alignment revision
suggestions.text: This course introduces students to the vital role of computers and computer programmers in shaping modern society. It aims to foster a strong foundation in logical formulation techniques essential for programming, while promoting the development of good coding practices. Students will be taught the fundamentals of Java programming: program structure and the JDK/JVM, console and file input/output, variables, data types and operators, conditional statements, loops, arrays, strings, methods and recursion, and connecting a Java program to a database. They will apply these to real-world problems. In line with La Consolacion University Philippines' commitment to forming Christo-centric Catholic professionals, the course integrates Marian Augustinian values in each lesson, ensuring that students not only achieve intellectual growth but also cultivate moral and ethical responsibility in the digital age. This holistic approach nurtures individuals who contribute positively to society, embodying community, humility, and love of service, as exemplified by the Blessed Virgin Mary and Saint Augustine. By the end of the course, students will have created their own Java applications, including a database-connected program, demonstrating both technical proficiency and a sense of purpose rooted in their Catholic faith.

findings.explanation: The description says only 'fundamentals of Java programming' and 'logical formulation techniques', which would fit any introductory Java course. It does not name the plan's main blocks: console input/output, file streams, conditionals and loops, arrays, strings, methods and recursion, and Java database connection. Its closing claim of 'created their own Java applications' is not tied to any plan content, such as the database-connected solution.
findings.recommendation: This course introduces students to the vital role of computers and computer programmers in shaping modern society. It aims to foster a strong foundation in logical formulation techniques essential for programming, while promoting the development of good coding practices. Students will be taught the fundamentals of Java programming: program structure and the JDK/JVM, console and file input/output, variables, data types and operators, conditional statements, loops, arrays, strings, methods and recursion, and connecting a Java program to a database. They will apply these to real-world problems. In line with La Consolacion University Philippines' commitment to forming Christo-centric Catholic professionals, the course integrates Marian Augustinian values in each lesson, ensuring that students not only achieve intellectual growth but also cultivate moral and ethical responsibility in the digital age. This holistic approach nurtures individuals who contribute positively to society, embodying community, humility, and love of service, as exemplified by the Blessed Virgin Mary and Saint Augustine. By the end of the course, students will have created their own Java applications, including a database-connected program, demonstrating both technical proficiency and a sense of purpose rooted in their Catholic faith.
